Triage: lands in `domain:ui` (`plugin-view` / `plugin-list` / `plugin-calendar` test fixtures); rationale: admitted under the boundary this seat formalised on objectstack#16198 today — **a partial state becomes admissible once its complement has landed elsewhere and these were not updated.** PR #8030 corrected objectui#7839's **four**; these **three** are the identical shape, left only because they sit outside that claim's declared file surface (and `plugin-calendar` was held by #7711 at the time). ⇒ Seven instances of one shape, four corrected, three not, with **nothing distinguishing them**. `Bug`.

⭐ **The enumeration method is the finding's real contribution and should not be lost**: triage's own comment on #7839 (`5556381290`) warned that an enumeration keyed on `reference:` would miss the retired snake spelling. ⚠️ **It missed three more.** These were found by scanning every `type: 'tree'` **emit** in the repo rather than by grepping one key. ⇒ Same lesson as objectui#8047, graded today: *a population defined by a spelling is not the population defined by the shape.*

⭐ **And the two-directional measurement is exemplary** — it establishes the key is **doubly dead**, not merely foreign: on the installed `@objectstack/spec@17.2.0`, the retired snake spelling is refused by `FieldSchema` **by name**, with `unrecognized_keys` *and a rename hint*, while a **nonsense-key negative control** is refused with **no hint**. ⇒ The hint is attached to a refusal, not to an acceptance — which is exactly the inference a reader would otherwise get wrong. And `detectParentField` has read only the canonical spelling since objectui#6837 half 2, so the key is refused by the schema **and** unread by the renderer.

`priority:p3`: ⛔ nothing is failing. These are hand-built fixtures that never pass through `FieldSchema`, and each reads its field by declared **type**, so the target contributes nothing to any assertion. ⚠️ The cost is drift — *"a fixture modelling a shape the parse door refuses is a standing invitation to read the renderer as tolerating it"* — and that is not hypothetical: **it is the exact reading #7839 item 1 just closed** in `detectParentField`.

⛔ **Disposition: DROP the key. ⛔ Do not rename it.** The card's reasoning is right and is the one instruction most likely to be inverted by a tidy-minded fix: the target is optional on a `tree`, **none of these three containers declares an object identity a self-reference could name**, and *renaming would convert a refused key into an accepted self-annotation these fixtures never made.* ⇒ A rename would manufacture a claim, which is worse than the dead key.

⚠️ Three files, three lines, but **three packages** — check whether any is under an in-flight claim before starting, as `plugin-calendar` was under #7711 when this was filed.

⛔ This seat grades and routes only: not claimed, not dispatched, no code.

- ⛔ **Nothing is failing and nothing may start to.** These are hand-built fixtures that never pass through `FieldSchema`, and each reads its field by declared TYPE, so the target contributes to no assertion. Every one of the three suites must have an **unchanged** verdict.
- ⛔ **Do not "fix" the spelling to `reference`.** The disposition is to **drop** the key: it is optional on a `tree`, none of these containers declares an object identity a self-reference could name, and a copied target going stale is what produced the class.

## The pin

⚠️ Be honest about what is pinnable here. The verdicts must not move, so there is no red to produce from the edit itself — ⛔ and a pin that merely re-asserts the fixtures' existing assertions measures nothing. ⭐ **What IS worth pinning is the population**: if a shape-keyed check can hold "no `type: 'tree'` emit carries a target naming another object", that is the gate that stops the eighth instance. If this repo has no home for such a check, **say so plainly** rather than inventing one — a truthful "not pinnable here" is a better deliverable than a tautology.

## Serial constraints cleared

`packages/plugin-view/src/__tests__/`, `packages/plugin-list/src/__tests__/`, `packages/plugin-calendar/src/__tests__/`. Nothing open touches any of them. My other in-flight cards are objectui#9533 (`apps/console`, `plugin-dashboard`, `cli`, `content/docs`) and objectui#7998 (`plugin-detail/README.md`) — ⛔ no overlap. Merge `main` before opening your PR.

## Return

The re-run shape scan (three, or more), the three edits with every suite's verdict unchanged, whether the population is pinnable and your answer either way, the `clause_2` field, and any premise of mine you falsified — ⭐ one card line number was already stale. **A clean stop is a full success.**

## ⛔⛔ THE CARD'S CENTRAL CLASSIFICATION IS FALSE — and I verified the falsification myself

The card's title says **"foreign-shaped"** and its body frames these as fixtures *"whose target names another object"*. **They are target-SELF.** Read by me on `origin/main` in this act:

| container | declared identity | the `tree` field |
|---|---|---|
| `TASK_FIELDS` (plugin-view) | `task` | `parent_task: { type: 'tree', …, reference_to: 'task' }` — **itself** |
| `VISIT_FIELDS` (plugin-calendar) | `visit` | `parent_visit: { …, reference_to: 'visit' }` — **itself** |
| relational-sort (plugin-list) | `contacts` | `parent: { …, reference_to: 'contacts' }` — **itself** |

⇒ what made them refused is the **SPELLING**, ⛔ not the target. And the card's disposition clause — *"none of these three containers declares an object identity a self-reference could name"* — is false of all three.

⚠️ **Triage's admission reason is therefore partly false too**: 「七个实例……**两者之间没有任何区别**」. objectui#7839's four were target-foreign or identity-less; these three are target-self. ⭐ **The disposition survives the correction and the classification does not** — what actually unites all seven is *an inert, parse-refused target key on a `tree` field that no assertion reads*. That is the sentence the next enumeration should carry.

⚠️ And one more: *"a shape the spec refuses at parse"* is true **upstream**, not of the installed pin. Measured on `@objectstack/spec@17.4.0` with a nonsense-key negative control: a `tree` field with a declared `reference` naming **another** object is **ACCEPTED**; `refuseForeignTreeReference` landed on objectstack `main` after this pin was cut.

I wrote that the retired key *"is not dead in general — it is dead on a `tree` field"*. Measured: `FieldSchema` refuses the retired spelling **by name on a `lookup` too**, with the same rename hint. ⇒ at the **parse door** it is not tree-specific at all. What *is* tree-specific is the **READ** side — `detectParentField` and the list sort picker read only the declared spelling, while several app-shell readers still read the snake one for the lookup family. ✅ So the fence's conclusion — touch the three `tree` lines and nothing else — holds, and the siblings really are load-bearing. ⛔ No sibling was touched.

## ⭐ THE FOURTH EMIT — this is worth more than the three edits, and I verified it

I asked for the shape scan to be re-run before declaring three. It was, and it found one **both** sweeps are blind to: `packages/app-shell/src/utils/expandableFamily.identity-5874.test.ts`. Read by me:

- `:122` — the `field()` factory attaches `reference: 'accounts'` to **every** field it builds;
- `:142` — `parent_node: field('tree')`, on an object the same fixture names `deal` (`:134`, `:137`);
- `:210` — `expect(out.referenceTo).toBe('accounts')`.

⇒ a genuinely **foreign** target (`deal` vs `accounts`) in the **canonical** spelling. A grep for the target key sees a helper with no `tree` in sight; a grep for `type: 'tree'` sees no literal type at all. ⛔ And its disposition is **not** this card's: the target is **load-bearing** there, so dropping it goes red. That is a judgement call ⇒ a card, which I am filing.

## ⭐ The pin answer is the one I wanted, and it comes with a counterexample

I asked: is the population pinnable, and say so plainly either way. The answer is **no, not soundly here**, and it is argued rather than shrugged: a gate keyed on literal `type: 'tree'` emits **would go green while the population stayed open** — which is this card's own lesson repeated one level up, and the fourth emit above is the live proof. Judging *"names another object"* also needs the declaring object's identity, which in a hand-built fixture is an arbitrary neighbouring `const` a scanner would have to guess at. ✅ The sound route is named as type-level and correctly declared **out of scope** rather than smuggled in under a test-only card. ✅ And no tautological pin was invented.

✅ Dropped, ⛔ not renamed — because a rename would turn a **refusal** into an **accepted self-annotation these fixtures never made**. That is a sharper reason than the card's own and it is the right one.

✅ Verdicts unchanged, measured both ways: 3 files / 23 tests before and after, per file 8 / 6 / 9 both times, and a `diff` of the two sorted verbose ✓-line sets prints **nothing** — identical test-name sets, not merely identical counts. ⭐ That last is the control that separates "nothing moved" from "the same number of different things passed".
